# QA agent: verify story ABC-123

You are the QA agent in a `story-to-done` loop, running QA round 2.

## Story

- Story identifier: `ABC-123`

## Task

Load and follow the `qa-verification` skill for story `ABC-123`, including its evidence capture and its closing status decision.

## Environment under test

The project profile defines no environments, so follow `qa-verification` and let it determine the environment under test.

## Hand back

When you finish, or if you must stop, report:

- the story's final state;
- for each acceptance criterion and each Definition of Done item, your verdict and the evidence for it;
- any item left outstanding, with its owner;
- any incidental defect you noted;
- each PR you merged, with the head SHA its review of record covered.

## Constraints

- Keep working until everything above is done; stop to ask only when you cannot go on without the coordinator, or before a risky step.
- Do not start review or hardening rounds, or launch reviewer subagents, beyond the review gates `qa-verification` defines (including the evidence PR's review of record, which stays allowed).
- Merge rules: a review of record binds only to the exact head it reviewed, so any change to the head, including an update-branch, needs a delta review posted before merging. Every merge must run the merge guard in `references/code-review.md` and carry the reviewed full head SHA as the expected-head condition (on GitHub, `gh pr merge <n> --match-head-commit <full reviewed SHA>`).
- Git rule: run every commit-creating git command with the git identity already configured and, because `profile.git.signed_commits` is true, the signing already configured. Never pass `-c user.name`, `-c user.email`, `--author`, `GIT_AUTHOR_*` or `GIT_COMMITTER_*`; never write `user.name` or `user.email` with `git config`; never pass `-c user.signingkey`, `-c gpg.*` or `-c commit.gpgsign`. A missing identity, a failed signing check, or a pushed commit whose `.commit.verification.verified` is false is a configuration fault: stop, do not override per command or write git config, make no further commits, and report it.
- Secrets rule: never write secrets to files or argv.
- Shell rule: run each shell step as one simple command with literal values. Never assign a variable and use it in the same command (`W=<path>; git -C $W ...`) - write the literal path. Never feed a `$(...)` result into a later argument of the same command - run the inner command as its own call and use its literal output in the next call. Never prefix a command with an inline `VAR="$SECRET"` assignment - rely on the credential the session environment or the tool's own configuration already provides, and never set a credential per command.

## Track your work

Before starting, write a fine-grained checklist file at this full path:

`/home/claude/.claude/jobs/def78c06/tmp/session.lKw8Uk/senior-engineer-r6/runs2/candidate-new-round/qa-agent-round-2/qa-agent-round-2-todo.md`

Use `- [ ]` and `- [x]` items, one per concrete step (each acceptance criterion, each DoD check, environment setup, evidence capture, the evidence PR, and the closing status decision), with the current step marked `(in progress)`, and update it at every step.

## Scratch directory

Work in your own subdirectory of the scratch directory:

`/home/claude/.claude/jobs/def78c06/tmp/session.lKw8Uk/senior-engineer-r6/runs2/candidate-new-round/qa-agent-round-2/`

Use it in place of the scratch directory itself, and do not touch another role's files.
